replace: # Security Guidelines
## Task-Relevant Security Checks
Apply checks relevant to the changed behavior and its trust boundaries within existing task scope:
- [ ] No hardcoded secrets (API keys, passwords, tokens)
- [ ] User inputs validated at relevant trust boundaries
- [ ] SQL injection prevention (parameterized queries with bound values)
- [ ] XSS prevention (sanitized HTML)
- [ ] CSRF protection for relevant state-changing requests
- [ ] Authentication/authorization verified for affected access paths
- [ ] Rate limiting where relevant to affected endpoints
- [ ] Error messages don't leak sensitive data
## Secret Management
- NEVER hardcode secrets in source code
- ALWAYS use environment variables or a secret manager
- Validate that required secrets are present at startup
- Rotate any secrets that may have been exposed through existing authorized secret-management procedures
## Security Response Protocol
If security issue found:
1. Identify affected behavior, severity, and trust boundary; avoid extending exposure
2. Fix the root cause within authorized task scope and verify the relevant security behavior
3. Rotate any exposed secrets through existing authorized secret-management procedures
4. Check directly related paths for the same failure mode within task scope
An independent audit is explicitly optional, including when a security issue is found. Finding an issue does not require an independent audit or expand task scope.
